summary: A mother tells her last-year-of-high-school daughter she will be away three nights a week and offers not to run.
realLife: When she was first persuaded to run for Congress, the future House leader's youngest child was about to start her senior year of high school. She told her daughter she would be away about three nights a week for several months and offered to stay out of the race if her daughter wanted her home. Her daughter said it was fine, and she said any teenager would feel the same.
gates: The candidate has a teenage child living in the household.
Someone has asked the candidate to run, or the candidate is weighing a filing.
weights: How close the candidate and child are.
Whether the child is in a school year that makes the parent's absence matter.
How much the child is told early.
inGame: Household members and a kin tie to a teen, a candidate weighing a filing, and a talk between parent and child could carry it; the candidate's nights away need a travel-time estimate in the campaign plan.

turns.what: The daughter asks her to stay, and the candidate declines to file this cycle.
turns.pulledBy: A close tie, a hard school year, fear of change.
turns.writesBack: No filing; candidate's tie with the daughter warms.

turns.what: The daughter shrugs and the candidate files with the house routine unchanged.
turns.pulledBy: An independent teen, other adults at home.

turns.what: The daughter says it was fine, then in the spring says she felt left out.
turns.pulledBy: A long campaign, missed school events.
turns.writesBack: Tie strain between parent and child; a missed-event note.
